legalName: Petition for Expungement or Resentencing of a Marijuana Conviction While Currently Serving (Mont. Code Ann. § 16-12-113(1)-(4), (8)-(12))
publicName: Marijuana conviction expungement or resentencing while serving a sentence
mechanism: Under § 16-12-113(1) a person currently serving a sentence for an act that is permitted under Title 16, chapter 12, or that is punishable by a lesser sentence under that chapter than the person was awarded, may petition for expungement or resentencing. Section 16-12-113(2) directs the court to presume the petitioner satisfies the criteria unless the county attorney provides a reasonable basis otherwise, and, where the criteria are satisfied, to grant the petition unless the court determines that granting it would pose an unreasonable risk of danger to public safety. Procedure is governed by the AF 22-0129 Temporary Rules, and the Office of the Court Administrator publishes Form A specifically for the currently-serving posture, with the same Certificate of Service and Proposed Order.

rationale: The registry declares outputStrategyDeclared 'composed' with compositionMode 'sequential' for this track, and both registry units carry outputStrategy 'official_pdf_fill'.

Adopted packet instruction on this track: “YES — STAGED OFFICIAL-FORM PACKET. OCA MMRTA Form A is expressly designed for the currently-serving posture. That posture is a scope restriction and a substantive-choice warning, not a reason to downgrade the mechanism to guidance.” The route therefore stays an official-form packet and no custom pleading is drafted in its place.

The Montana state pack records the same conclusion: “Montana provides official self-represented packets (misdemeanor; MMRTA marijuana) plus a DOJ removal request, so these map to official forms rather than a custom pleading.”
Every court document in this route is an Office of the Court Administrator or Department of Justice form. Drafting a substitute would displace a controlling official form.

authoritySpine.description: Decriminalized acts; petition for expungement, resentencing or redesignation. Subsection (1) is the currently-serving pathway; subsection (2) supplies the presumption, the county-attorney reasonable-basis rebuttal and the public-safety override; subsections (3)-(4) constrain any resentencing.
Defines an expungement or resentencing of marijuana conviction court.
Authorises appointment of a decriminalized marijuana conviction expungement judge with the authority and power of an elected district court judge.
Completes the expungement or resentencing of marijuana conviction court structure.

Order adopting Temporary Rules for Expungement, Resentencing, or Redesignation under the MMRTA, filed 15 March 2022. The order was retrieved; the attached rules were not. URL: https://courts.mt.gov/external/forms/mmrta/af22-0129order.pdf
The Montana Marijuana Regulation and Taxation Act as enacted by initiative and amended by session law; the source of the decriminalization the petition relies on.

The person whose records are being expunged, not the court and not the clerk, must send the order to the arresting agency, the prosecutor, the clerk and the Department of Justice, together with fingerprints and the DOJ form. This is why the route has a second, participant-initiated Department of Justice stage.

authoritySpine.description: Terminology control. Expungement means to permanently destroy, delete or erase a record from the criminal history record information system maintained by the Department of Justice. What happens at the courts, law-enforcement agencies and prosecutors' offices is sealing, not destruction (§ 46-18-1110(2)(a)). Removal is the DOJ term for deleting a non-conviction record. Redesignation and resentencing are MMRTA outcomes and are neither.

counselFlags.statement: The text of the Temporary Rules adopted by Montana Supreme Court order AF 22-0129 was not retrieved — only the order was. The rules govern procedure for this track and may contain filing, service or hearing requirements not reflected on the OCA forms. Relatedly, whether the 21-day county attorney response window is stated in the Temporary Rules or is OCA guidance only is unresolved; it is currently sourced to the OCA instructions.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: Obtain the AF 22-0129 Temporary Rules text and reconcile every filing, service and hearing requirement in this route against it, including the source of the 21-day window.

counselFlags.statement: Which CRISS Expungement/Removal Request Form version the Department of Justice enforces in practice, and what the current required attachment set is, is unresolved. The 2023 PDF requires valid photo identification for two request types and the “Original Court Order” for misdemeanour expungement; the 29 April 2024 DOCX drops the photo-ID requirement, requires the “Original Court Judgement” instead, and adds “Deferred Prosecution” to the fourth request type.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: Which version and attachment set CRISS enforces. Until confirmed, the fail-closed reading is used: photo identification is included by default and a certified copy of the judgment is requested.

counselFlags.statement: Whether any Montana district, justice, municipal or city court imposes a local form, local cover sheet or local addendum for this route is unresolved and material. Both the OCA MMRTA instructions and the deferred-dismissal guidance expressly warn of local variation, and the OCA instructions direct the participant to the Court Locator for local rules.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: Whether a local form, cover sheet or addendum exists at the participant's sentencing court. This route asserts no cover sheet and builds the local-rules lookup as a required participant step.

counselFlags.statement: Whether an expunged Montana conviction may lawfully be denied in response to a general inquiry is unresolved. No Montana perjury shield or restoration-to-prior-status provision was located in Title 46 chapter 18 part 11, § 46-18-204 or § 44-5-202. Nothing in this route says anything about denial; the question is treated as a hard self-help stop.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: Whether a Montana perjury shield or restoration provision exists before any participant-facing statement about denying a cleared record is written.

counselFlags.statement: Master Library Edition 1.1 retains the CRISS Expungement/Removal Request Form as a SUPPORTING_PROCESS asset with document role SUPPORTING_FORM, not as a packet form. The authority gate treats a supporting-process asset as one that cannot back an official_pdf_fill component, so this route's DOJ-stage component is recorded as an authority role mismatch. The classification is the issue, not the mechanism: the form is a genuine Department of Justice agency form, it carries no use restriction, and it is the required and only vehicle for the DOJ stage.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: Reclassification of the CRISS form as a packet form in a successor Master Library edition. Edition 1.1 is not modified.

counselFlags.statement: Master Library Edition 1.1 gives the OCA MMRTA Proposed Order and the OCA MMRTA Certificate of Service the same document ID, MT-OCA-MMRTA, distinguished only by document role ORDER against SERVICE. They are two different binaries with two different SHA-256 values, so a component naming MT-OCA-MMRTA matches two retained assets carrying conflicting hashes and the authority gate records an authority hash conflict.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That each form receives its own document ID in a successor edition before either component becomes resolver-selectable. Both mappings are retained and the track stays authority-gated in the meantime.

counselFlags.statement: Whether the § 16-12-113(7) no-hearing default applies to a petition under subsection (1) is unresolved. By its terms subsection (7) addresses applications under subsection (5), the completed-sentence pathway. Form A nonetheless includes the same hearing election. This route presents the election as the form does and does not assert that no hearing will be held.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: Whether the no-hearing default reaches a subsection (1) petition, before any participant-facing statement about hearings is written.

counselFlags.statement: Whether any decriminalized marijuana conviction expungement judge has been appointed under § 16-12-115, and if so whether that changes the practical filing destination in any county, is unresolved. Sections 16-12-114 through 16-12-116 create the structure; whether it has been used is not established.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: Whether such a judge has been appointed anywhere in Montana and what it does to the filing destination. This route names no court and asserts only that the filing goes to the court that sentenced the participant.

counselFlags.statement: Custody status alone is an attorney-handoff trigger for this track, and LegalEase does not represent an incarcerated participant in court. The practical filing and service obstacles facing an incarcerated participant — how a person in custody obtains the DOJ criminal record and court documents, files in the sentencing court and serves the county attorney — were not resolved by the source review.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: The delivery path for an incarcerated participant before this route is offered to one. This track's gating condition is that the participant is still serving, so the handoff trigger will fire often.

counselFlags.statement: Section 16-12-113(2) lets the court refuse relief where granting the petition would pose an unreasonable risk of danger to public safety. That override is unique to this track and does not appear in the subsection (6) completed-sentence pathway. Any case where it is plausibly in play is a handoff. Nothing in this route authors a public-safety argument or any assertion that relief would not pose such a risk.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That screening detects when the override is plausibly in play and routes to an attorney rather than producing a packet.

counselFlags.statement: LegalEase does not choose between expungement and resentencing. These are materially different outcomes with different consequences, the form requires the participant to choose, and the election is the participant's alone. Any analysis of which outcome is better is legal advice and triggers handoff. No resentencing computation appears anywhere in this route: § 16-12-113(3) and (4) require credit for time served, prohibit supervision after resentencing, prohibit a term longer than the original sentence and prohibit reinstatement of charges dismissed under a negotiated plea agreement, and computing the result is legal work.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That the outcome election is presented as the form presents it and never pre-selected, and that no resentencing arithmetic is generated.

counselFlags.statement: Whether the historical conduct is now permitted, or now punishable by a lesser sentence, under Title 16, chapter 12 requires mapping decades-old charging language and quantities against the current chapter, and it is the central legal question of the track. LegalEase presents the enumerated statutory list and the participant selects; the free-text specify-offence path is an attorney handoff, not a completion path.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That the free-text offence path routes to an attorney and never produces a packet.

counselFlags.statement: The Montana Legal Services Association / Montana Supreme Court Access to Justice Commission forms, including the Statement of Inability to Pay Court Costs and Fees, are stamped “© 2025 … This form may be used for non-commercial purposes only.” Expungement.ai is a paid product, so reproducing or distributing them inside a packet is a commercial use. They are drafting references only: never generated, never relabelled, never converted, never lightly rewritten, never runtime-selectable and never generation_allowed.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That the fee-waiver unit remains a link-out unless a licence is obtained. The restriction changes source use, not the existence of the mechanism.

counselFlags.statement: No filing-fee amount is asserted anywhere in this route. The registry states only that the participant is responsible for filing fees and costs and that the fee depends on the court level. The Montana state pack records the same gap: “The reference does not state a fixed District Court filing-fee amount for the misdemeanor expungement or marijuana petitions; confirm the current fee with the filing court (source gap — no fee schedule provided in the Nationwide source).”
counselFlags.mustConfirm: The current filing fee at each Montana court level before any fee figure is shown to a participant. No fee is charged for the CRISS request.

counselFlags.statement: Court name, county, docket/case number, judge, county attorney and county attorney position are left blank throughout this route. The only sourced venue statement is that the filing goes to the court that sentenced the participant, on the three caption options the form offers (Montana district court, justice court, or municipal or city court), and that the county attorney for the county in which the petition is filed must be served. Whether a designated § 16-12-115 judge changes that destination is unresolved.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That every court and party identity comes from the participant's own screening answers and court paperwork and is prefilled from no other source.

counselFlags.statement: Montana's words are not interchangeable and participant copy must keep them apart. Expungement under § 46-18-1103(1) means to permanently destroy, delete or erase a record from the criminal history record information system maintained by the Department of Justice. What happens at the courts, law-enforcement agencies and prosecutors' offices is sealing, not destruction (§ 46-18-1110(2)(a)). Removal is the DOJ term for deleting a non-conviction record. Redesignation and resentencing are MMRTA outcomes and are neither.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That every participant-facing string in this route is checked against the four-term distinction before release.

counselFlags.statement: One complete form set per conviction, never a consolidated petition. The OCA instructions require a separate form for each conviction even where the convictions occurred at the same time. This is the opposite of the Montana misdemeanour expungement track, where one petition covers the whole record, and the rules engine must not generalise across the two.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That the generator emits one complete unit set per conviction and never merges convictions into a single petition.

omissionProof.statement: units[] enumerates every legal unit the pinned registry entry and the compiled MT profile record for this track. The registry records two ordered stages in units[] — the court petition stage and the conditional DOJ CRISS stage — and six packetSet components across them: primary_filing (MMRTA Form A), certificate_of_service, proposed_order, attachment, conditional primary_filing (CRISS form) and instructions. Each of those six is a distinct legal unit here, one per required output. A seventh unit is added for the one further legal unit the registry records outside packetSet: the filing fee, or in its place the statement of inability to pay court costs and fees, which the registry lists both as a participant filing requirement required before filing and as a conditional apply_fee_waiver participant action. Nothing else in the registry entry or the compiled profile describes a document, form, letter or cover sheet for this track. No pleading_document unit exists because every court document in the route is a controlling official Office of the Court Administrator or Department of Justice form; no agency_request_letter unit exists because the Department of Justice stage runs on the official CRISS form rather than a drafted letter; and no cover_sheet unit exists because neither source records one — whether any Montana court imposes a local cover sheet is an unresolved release blocker carried as a counsel flag, not a drafted component.

profilePassageReferenced.passage: For marijuana-related cases, the Montana Judicial Branch provides: MMRTA Form A Currently serving sentence; request expungement or resentencing / MMRTA Form B Sentence completed; request expungement or redesignation / Proposed Order Submitted with petition / Certificate of Service Shows service on county attorney. … The Judicial Branch says the person must know the date or approximate date of conviction, the Montana court where it occurred, and must attach a copy of the criminal record from Montana DOJ. … Montana Judicial Branch says a separate form must be completed for each conviction, even if the convictions happened at the same time. … The petition must be served on the county attorney for the county where the petition is filed. … If the court grants marijuana-related expungement, the petitioner must file the DOJ Expungement/Removal Request Form with the Montana Department of Justice along with the court order.
profilePassageReferenced.reading: The compiled profile enumerates exactly the same document set this route contains for the currently-serving posture: Form A (Form B belongs to the separate completed-sentence track and is excluded here), the Proposed Order, the Certificate of Service, the DOJ criminal-record attachment, and the conditional DOJ Expungement/Removal Request Form after a grant. The profile records nothing further.
